hooks.command: cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" && git add -A && git diff --cached --quiet || { git commit -q -m "auto: update via Claude Code" -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git push -q origin HEAD; }

hooks.statusMessage: Checking CLAUDE.md against this PR's diff...
hooks.prompt: A GitHub PR was just created for this repo (cd "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" first). Before the user reviews/merges it, check whether CLAUDE.md needs updating to reflect what THIS PR actually changed. Find the PR's base (usually main) and run `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- . ':!CLAUDE.md'` to see the full diff — use that as your primary signal, reading only as much surrounding code as needed to understand it; don't re-scan the whole repo against all of CLAUDE.md. 'Doc-worthy' means: new commands/architecture/top-level files, a bumped service-worker cache version, or a real logic/behavior change to a function CLAUDE.md already describes (added/removed/changed parameter, changed call signature, changed control flow, changed data shape). If something is doc-worthy, edit CLAUDE.md and commit+push that fix to the same branch (so it lands in the PR) with a plain message like 'Sync CLAUDE.md with this PR'. If nothing is doc-worthy, do nothing and exit quietly — do not touch CLAUDE.md, do not comment on the PR, do not merge anything.
